title: Authentication: session, token and JWT in both frameworks

videos.script: Every request answers one question before anything else: who is asking. {{title}} It starts with a password, and what the server keeps of it. Not the password. A slow hash, with a salt. Hash the same password twice, and you get two different strings. {{hash}} Then three ways to remember a person between requests. A session is a random key in a cookie and a row on the server. Log out, and the row is gone, so the old cookie leads nowhere. {{session}} A DRF token is a key in a header, for scripts and apps. It is kept in a table, as it was sent. Whoever reads that table can be anyone in it. {{token}} And a JWT carries its own claims, signed. You decode one with base64 and no key at all. It is signed, not encrypted. Change one letter, and the signature fails. {{jwt}} There is also a trap at the login form. If an unknown name answers faster than a known one, the form tells strangers who has an account. You measure it, and fix it with a decoy hash. {{decoy}} Last, how to choose. Sessions for a browser and its own site. Tokens in a table for programs. And a short-lived JWT when several services must trust one issuer.
